title: Pressure injury stages

findings.where: pressure-injury.jsx: stageFrom(), PRESSURE_CONTEXT, TIED_AFTER, unsettled(); PressureInjuryDiagram params.stage outline
findings.title: Stage extraction can falsely assert a current pressure injury
findings.problem: These inputs produce incorrect stage selections: (1) "The client is at risk for a stage 4 pressure injury." returns {stage: 4}, although no injury is asserted. (2) "The client has stage 3 sacral sarcoma and a Braden score of 12." returns {stage: 3}: Braden supplies the supposed pressure context, "sacral" supplies the stage attachment, and sarcoma escapes the disease exclusion list. (3) "The client has a stage 4 pressure injury. That diagnosis was ruled out on reassessment." still returns {stage: 4}, because the exclusion occurs in a separate sentence without a stage keyword. Each result can outline a pressure-injury stage that is hypothetical, unrelated, or explicitly excluded.
findings.fix: Prefer reviewed, structured metadata identifying the current pressure-injury stage; otherwise return null. If text extraction remains, require an affirmative stage assertion explicitly attached to a pressure injury—not merely a risk score, generic wound, or anatomical location—and handle uncertainty and cross-sentence exclusions conservatively. Add all three examples as regression tests expecting null.

assessment: Hold publication. The text parser can generate a patient-specific pressure-injury stage that the stem does not establish.
